title: The Mirror Crack'd - touring - review
transcript: the Wales Millennium Centre and Wiltshire creative touring production of Agatha Christie's than their cracked adapted for the stage by Rachel Wagstaff and directed by Nelly still premiered at Salisbury Playhouse now this could have been a standard Agatha Christie whodunit but it was far above standard and for this we should thank Rachel Wagstaff she's done an adaptation that's reasonably faithful to the plot and characters just simplified really it's still a story featuring Miss Marple and the thrust of it is that a movie star moves into the village and I was a party someone dies drinking the Stars daiquiri it's already a story in which Miss Marple is musing on old age and changing times it's set in the early sixties but what Rachel Wagstaff has added along with racier sharper dialogue our extra deaths in which loneliness is considered and also memory not only the memories which make us what we are but also the unreliable memory because we see scenes re-enacted as various people recall them slightly differently it's a simple setting which enables the flashbacks and the changes of scene to work quickly and smoothly in plane Miss Marple Suzie Blake has a lot of weighty predecessors to live up to but I have to say she holds her own in an excellent performance all the Carson's are eleven of them are very good I particularly mentioned Simon Shepard who plays the slightly pompous and very patronizing inspector Julia Hills as Miss Marple snobbish friend and Susanna Hamilton who plays the fragile film style they had humour to the parts as well as gravitas you know I can't actually fault this production I had a really good evening and I give them their cracked 5 stars if you found this review interesting useful please subscribe to my youtube channel a mini theatre views by clicking on the icon you know you
